newsitem.title: THAILAND: Standard Chartered upbeat on Hong Kong handover.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered upbeat on Hong Kong handover.

text.p: Britain's Standard Chartered Bank remains upbeat about business prospects in Hong Kong after the territory returns to China on July 1, the bank's senior executives said on Monday.
"I am quite optimistic about what is going to happen," the bank's Group Chief Executive Malcolm Williamson said at a function held by British Chamber of Commerce in Bangkok on Monday.
The bank derived about 30 percent of its 1996 profits in Asia from its Hong Kong operations last year, he said.
Standard Chartered's total Asian operations accounted for about 70 percent of the bank's 870 million sterling in pre-tax profits last year, Williamson said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule in 50 days, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
"It's not a case of being worried about Hong Kong, which I am not, or trying to reduce our investment there...we would like to continue to develop our business in Hong Kong and China," he added.
The bank had recently found premises in Shanghai's Pudong New Area in China and hoped to begin local currency operations before the end of the year, a bank spokesman added.

"When I joined I thought our exposure to Hong Kong was disproportionate to elsewhere and I tried very hard to correct that by growing other parts of our Asian business more quickly ... but as fast as we grew our business in south Asia we grew our business in Hong Kong equally fast," Williamson said.
He said talks with other banks allowing them access to Standard Chartered's extensive Asian network were progressing.

"There are a number of other discussions going on but because most of these deals are fairly bespoke they take time to come to fruition. We are talking to a number of people on the continent about it," Williamson said.
The firm has already formed ventures in Asia with Australia's Westpac Banking Corp, Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, First Chicago NBD Corp and Fleet Financial Services.

Recent market talk that Standard Chartered could be interested in even closer ties with Westpac after a recent relaxation of foreign ownership laws in the Australian banking sector was unfounded, Williamson said.
